plugins.name: DocGuard

Produces a Low / Medium / High risk badge per question and a detailed per-student report with signal-by-signal evidence. Works with Moodle™ Assignment activity (file submissions).

plugins.name: Site Down Alert
plugins.description: Two-part downtime intelligence system. The Moodle plugin runs a cron task every 5 minutes detecting early warning signs (high DB latency, memory pressure, disk near-full, cron stalled) and emails your configured alert address before a crash. Configure your alert email in Site Admin → Plugins → Local plugins → Site Down Alert. It also exposes a lightweight /local/downalert/ping.php health endpoint returning a JSON status report for UptimeRobot or your own monitoring. The included standalone server monitor script runs on your server via crontab every 3 minutes — when a site goes completely down it diagnoses the exact cause (TIMEOUT, SSL_EXPIRED, DNS_FAILURE, CONNECTION_REFUSED, HTTP_500, PHP-FPM pool exhausted, disk full, OOM, stuck cron) and emails your configured address with the root cause summary and exact SSH commands to fix it immediately.

plugins.name: Student Email Manager
plugins.description: Automatically provision and manage cPanel email accounts for every Moodle student. Supports UAPI (preferred) with XML API v2 fallback. Auto-creates accounts on enrolment, auto-suspends on user suspension, auto-archives on deletion, auto-restores on reactivation. Admin dashboard shows live stats (total, active, missing, suspended, archived, errors) with per-student actions and bulk operations. Students get a 'My Email' navigation item that shows their college email address, masked password (reveal + copy), and a direct link to Roundcube webmail. Four email format options: auto-number with prefix (e.g. stu0001), Moodle username, student ID, or firstname.lastname. Passwords AES-256-CBC encrypted at rest using a site-derived key. Note: cPanel/Roundcube is not an OAuth/SAML provider — SSO via auto-POST is not used (Roundcube CSRF protection blocks it). The portal instead shows credentials for the student to copy into Roundcube. For IMAP-based Moodle login using college email credentials, use auth_imap alongside this plugin.

plugins.name: Student Email IMAP Auth
plugins.description: Lets students log into Moodle using their provisioned college email address and mailbox password, verified in real-time via IMAP against the cPanel mail server. Works alongside Student Email Manager (local_studentemail). Supports login with full email address (stu0001@students.college.edu.au) or Moodle username. Only active provisioned accounts are accepted — suspended or archived students cannot log in even with a correct password. Staff and admins are completely unaffected (plugin silently falls through for users with no provisioned email). Configurable IMAP host, port, SSL/TLS encryption, certificate validation skip (for cPanel self-signed certs), and connection timeout. Requires PHP imap extension on the Moodle server.
